raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

MRV2 pooling can avoid per-step overhead when decoder prompts are split across prefill chunks. Intermediate chunks with no finished requests still creates a blocking CUDA event, entering the output copy stream, and synchronized
when the empty output was consumed. Token-wise `ALL` pooling also cloned every partial hidden-state chunk into a Python list and concatenated the chunks when the request finished. 

This PR adds a no-output fast path that returns the known `None` results without copy-stream/event work, and replaces the `ALL` chunk list with one prompt-sized buffer populated in place. The result is **1.1-1.6%** higher request throughput and 1.1-1.4% lower median E2E latency in the tested MRV2 chunked-pooling workloads, without changing model outputs.

The `ALL` path retains its single-chunk fast path: requests that finish in one step still return the original hidden-state view, cloning only when async scheduling requires owned storage. Multi-chunk requests allocate once, copy each chunk once, and return the populated view without a final `torch.concat`.

## Reproducer

Hardware: NVIDIA H100 80GB. Model runner V2 was forced for every server with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`. Each result is the median of three runs after 16 warmup requests, using 256 measured requests at an infinite request rate.

### `LAST`

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
  vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B \
  --runner pooling \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \
  --api-server-count 1 \
  --port 8000
```

```bash
for concurrency in 16 32; do
  for run in 1 2 3; do
    vllm bench serve \
      --backend openai-embeddings \
      --model Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B \
      --endpoint /v1/embeddings \
      --dataset-name random \
      --random-input-len 4096 \
      --random-output-len 128 \
      --num-prompts 256 \
      --num-warmups 16 \
      --request-rate inf \
      --max-concurrency "${concurrency}" \
      --seed 17 \
      --save-result \
      --result-filename "last-c${concurrency}-r${run}.json"
  done
done
```

### `ALL`

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
  vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B \
  --runner pooling \
  --pooler-config '{"task":"token_embed"}' \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --max-model-len 2048 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 256 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \
  --api-server-count 1 \
  --port 8000
```

```bash
for concurrency in 16 32; do
  for run in 1 2 3; do
    vllm bench serve \
      --backend vllm-pooling \
      --model Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B \
      --endpoint /pooling \
      --dataset-name random \
      --random-input-len 1024 \
      --random-output-len 128 \
      --num-prompts 256 \
      --num-warmups 16 \
      --request-rate inf \
      --max-concurrency "${concurrency}" \
      --seed 17 \
      --extra-body '{"encoding_format":"bytes"}' \
      --save-result \
      --result-filename "all-c${concurrency}-r${run}.json"
  done
done
```

## Output on main / on branch

The following values are medians of the three saved `vllm bench` JSON results.
Positive throughput deltas and negative latency deltas are improvements.

| Pooling | Concurrency | Main req/s | Branch req/s | Throughput | Main median E2E | Branch median E2E | Median E2E | Main p99 E2E | Branch p99 E2E | p99 E2E |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `LAST` | 16 | 29.209 | 29.593 | +1.31% | 546.575 ms | 539.395 ms | -1.31% | 548.717 ms | 543.803 ms | -0.90% |
| `LAST` | 32 | 29.196 | 29.506 | +1.06% | 1092.249 ms | 1079.039 ms | -1.21% | 1097.558 ms | 1087.089 ms | -0.95% |
| `ALL` | 16 | 30.078 | 30.475 | +1.32% | 529.486 ms | 523.631 ms | -1.11% | 530.385 ms | 525.227 ms | -0.97% |
| `ALL` | 32 | 29.934 | 30.404 | +1.57% | 1063.921 ms | 1048.531 ms | -1.45% | 1067.525 ms | 1052.183 ms | -1.44% |

Model-accuracy coverage used the existing chunked-pooling comparison suite. It checks Qwen3 decoder token embeddings (`ALL`) against Hugging Face, Qwen3 sequence embeddings (`LAST`) against Hugging Face, and Qwen3-Reranker `LAST` scores with chunked prefill against an unchunked reference.

Main output (verbatim):

```text
================== 3 passed, 16 warnings in 148.56s (0:02:28) ==================
```

Branch output (verbatim):

```text
================== 3 passed, 16 warnings in 133.45s (0:02:13) ==================
```

Both revisions passed the same accuracy gates; no model-output regression was observed within the existing test tolerances.

## Test Plan

Run on both main (`9c8e90eb2637a863ca14e47fd436b10ed7ba6536`) and this branch with an H100:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/language/pooling/test_all_pooling_plus_chunked_prefill.py -vv
```

```text
main:   3 passed, 16 warnings in 148.56s
branch: 3 passed, 16 warnings in 133.45s
```

## AI assistance disclosure

OpenAI Codex (GPT-5) assisted with drafting the code. All changed lines were human-reviewed by the submitter, and all reported tests and benchmarks were human-run.

nodes.body:
All credit to Codex Sol for back of the napkin calculations below: 

The allocation is exactly:

```text
prompt_len × hidden_size × element_size
In the ALL reproducer, that is 1024 × 1024 × 2 = 2 MiB per active partial request. With four 256-token chunks, a deterministic H100 allocation probe measured:
- main: 4.0 MiB peak—the final 2 MiB concat coexists with cached chunks
- branch: 2.5 MiB peak—the 2 MiB buffer coexists with the current 0.5 MiB chunk
Thus the pooling-state peak is 1.5 MiB lower for this workload, although the branch allocates the full 2 MiB earlier.
```
More generally, live buffer memory is Σ(prompt_len × hidden_size × element_size) across concurrent partial ALL requests. Therefore, very long or concurrently capped prefills could increase steady-state memory even though the final-concat peak is removed. I’ll document this tradeoff; alternatively, we can grow the buffer incrementally if we want to avoid the up-front allocation.

The model’s hidden size is 1024 and it runs BF16, confirming the 2 MiB calculation ([configuration](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B/blob/main/config.json)).
